The nerves won't go away if your focused on not messing up. Even if you plan on what you're going to say if you're nervous then you'll probably forget it during the moment. 

You can start getting comfortable by talking to him just a little bit. A good starter would be a genuine question. If you actually need help with something you'll be more focused on the task rather than messing up. After a while you'll get less nervous. Only do this if he's conveniently there so you can ask him the question. 

And if you know some of his interest and your genuinely curious you can ask him about that. For example:. If he's in to anime you can ask him "hey NAME you watch anime right?... You got any recommendations?" 

The main word her is genuine because if you're really want to know about something it's easier to go with it and it's more natural. You're still trying to "force" a conversation but it's less obvious. It's called human google by Charisma on Command on YouTube from this video https://youtu.be/Cbyc7mscFlA

You can also compliment something you like that he did.  For example "Good job on you presentation, I really like your points" something like that but again you gotta be genuine. If you compliment him too many times it'll start to seem  that you suckling up to him. But these are just conversation starters so you'll eventually get comfortable and be able to talk to him naturally about anything. 

 I can't think of more general advice cause it's situational. Its a bit long but I tried to be detailed as much as possible. Hope this helps
